senses.gloss: m. (deriv. of אַכְסַנְיָא) stranger, guest, lodger; also (ξένος) hired soldier.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 2:8:3">Y. Erub. II, end 20ᵇ</cite> <he>יֵעָשֶׂה כא׳</he> let him be considered as a stranger (transient lodger).
Tosef. Shebi. V, 21 אכסנא some ed. (ed. Zuck. אַכְסְנָיִין pl.) soldier, v. אַכְסַנְיָא 3).—

<cite ref="Arakhin 16b:78">Ib.</cite> <he>א׳ פוגם ונפגם</he> a traveller (constantly changing his lodging place) discredits others a. himself; a. fr.—Pl. <he>אַכְסְנָיִין</he> (v. supra), <he>אַכְסְנִין</he> <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 27">Lev. R. s. 27</cite>.—<cite ref="A01737"><he>אַכְסְנֵי</he></cite>, <cite ref="A01739"><he>אַכְסְנַיָּא</he></cite>, <cite ref="A01737"><he>אַכְסְנָאֵי</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Genesis 47:21">Targ. Y. II, Gen. XLVII, 21</cite> <he>א׳ גילולאי</he> exiled strangers.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 50">Gen. R. s. 50</cite> <he>הב לאילין א׳</he> give these travellers &c.—*<he>אַכְסָנִים</he>.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 10">Num. R. s. 10</cite> (p. 239ᶜ ed. Amst.) <he>מנהג הא׳</he> custom of hospitality [prob. <cite ref="A01739"><he>אכסניא</he></cite>].
